_comment: Page copy for /g/uk-geo, written 28 Nov 2026: GEO alone at a fixed monthly price, from £1,000 a month (the owner, 28 Nov 2026). No ChatGPT ads in the package and no ad figures on the page. /g/uk-ai-visibility, which sells GEO with ChatGPT ads from £1,500, is a different page and is not changed by this one. The case is a Norwegian private clinic group and is not named: the owner's rule of 27 Nov 2026 is that every client is anonymous in marketing. Figures: AI assistant bookings are booking_completed in the group's Google Analytics (property 419601371), Norwegian pages, all AI sources: Sept to 27 Nov 2026 is 8 + 10 + 17 = 35, Sept to Nov 2025 is 2 + 0 + 1 = 3. The measurement is Search Atlas analysis ff77201a, run 28 Nov 2026: 20 Norwegian questions without the clinic's name, put to ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode; named in 42 of 58 answers (ChatGPT 13 of 18, two answers came back empty; Gemini 14 of 20; AI Mode 15 of 20), in at least one answer on 18 of 20 questions. It is one run with no earlier measurement, so the page never says 'from x% to 72%'. A new website launched in August 2026, the month the rise began, and the page says the two cannot be separated. Market figures: Which?, December 2025 (Yonder, 4,189 UK adults, 10 to 14 Sept 2025); OpenAI's head of ChatGPT, February 2026. The build refuses dashes, exclamation marks and American spellings. Nothing here may describe commission.

strip.tail: The client is a private clinic group in Norway with several sites. From February 2026 we worked on its site for search and AI assistants: around 30 articles, about 150 page titles and descriptions, and mentions on the third-party sites AI tools read. A new website went live in August 2026, the month the rise began, and we cannot separate its effect from the rest of the work. AI assistants did send a few visitors before we started, so this is from barely visible, not from nothing.

how.intro: One package, run by one team, reported once a month.

items.p: In the first month we track 25 questions your buyers ask across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI Mode, see who is named instead of you, and fix what stops AI tools reading your site.
Every month, four pages written to answer those questions, and work to get you named on the third-party sites AI tools trust: trade directories, industry press and review sites.
We put the same 25 questions to the AI tools again each month and count the enquiries from AI assistants in your own analytics, so you can see whether it is working.

items.q: Is this just SEO with a new name?
items.a: Partly. AI assistants read the same web as Google, so a site that is easy to read and well referenced helps both. What is new is that an AI answer names a few companies instead of listing ten, and leans heavily on third-party sources. We work on both.

items.q: How soon will we see anything?
items.a: Expect months, not weeks. For the clinic group the work started in February 2026 and the rise in bookings came in the autumn. How long it takes for you depends on how strong your competitors are.
No. An AI answer changes from one person and one day to the next, so nobody can honestly promise a position. We track the same questions every month, so you can see whether it is working.

items.q: Your case is a Norwegian clinic group. Why would this work for us?
items.a: ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI Mode give UK and Norwegian buyers the same kind of answer, built from the same kind of sources. What differs is the competition, and we go through that on the first call. We have not yet measured a UK client over the same length of time, and we would rather say so.

items.q: Do you run ChatGPT ads as well?
items.a: Not as part of this package. This is the unpaid work: being named in the answer itself.

items.q: What if we want to stop?
items.a: Give 30 days' notice by email. You keep the content and the measurements.
